problems.title: The evaluator ignores candidate text after its character cutoff
claim: `traditional_evaluator.py`, `evaluate_result`, slices the candidate to its first two hundred characters before all traditional metrics, while retaining the complete reference.
analysis: An identical \(639\)-character, \(80\)-word answer can be truncated to \(25\) words. With perfect unigram matches on that prefix, BLEU’s brevity penalty is \(\exp(1-80/25)=e^{-2.2}\approx0.110803\), rather than \(1\). Any changed suffix beyond the cutoff is invisible.
result: The released function does not score complete long answers. Original prediction files and exact experiment versions are needed for publication-wide impact.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Remove the character slice or declare and apply a justified symmetric evaluation policy. No recovered benchmark score is supplied.
problems.impact_rationale: The public scorer is defective on long outputs; its original scientific effect is unquantified.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Inference cache identity omits the task
claim: `eval_spatial_llana.py`, `main`, creates a model-basename/split output file and returns if it exists before reading the task-specific data selector.
analysis: Brief captions, detailed captions and single-round answers on the same split therefore share a filename and can reuse an earlier task’s output. Model and split alone do not identify the inference request.
result: The public cache key is incomplete. No claim that the authors reused wrong predictions in the reported tables is established.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Include task identity and validate model/checkpoint, dataset revision and generation settings before cache reuse.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a released caching boundary, without established historical result contamination.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The fine-tuning gaps exceed the stated universal one-point bound
problems.source_location: Section 6, p. 9, Table 6 discussion; Table 5, p. 8.
claim: Section 6 says frozen-LLM variants stay within one point across reported metrics.
analysis: Table 6’s unambiguous question-answering gaps are \(1.06\), \(1.05\), \(1.50\) and \(1.50\) percentage points. These exceed the literal universal bound. Spatial columns differ between Tables 5 and 6 and cannot be reconciled from the inspected text alone.
result: The quantitative summary needs narrowing. The broader observation that freezing retains much performance can remain true.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a small table-summary discrepancy, not a reversal of the central performance claim.
problems.existing_correction_status: No validated correction is established for this item.
